threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask where to find 'real' coffee instead of just knowing it’s around every corner from the 24-hour bagel shop.
Last night on the 35, a guy dressed as a banana argued with the driver about the legitimacy of fruit-themed disguises. We laughed all the way to Norwood.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a suit arguing with a dog over a tram seat. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM serving more locals than tourists, complete with a terrace full of art students chatting about philosophy.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell someone’s a local if they know to avoid the BART platform at Civic Center on nights when the train breaks down—like clockwork.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full business attire casually reading a novel on the 19 bus while a street musician played Mozart outside. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the Mercat de l'Abaceria is just a market for souvenirs. It’s actually where locals grab the freshest produce and gossip at dawn.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the local bus maps—most locals know that the best way is just to follow the crowd.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line' and look baffled when locals refer to the 'food scene' without mentioning the market.
Caught a guy singing opera on the 59 last night. Sounded like a proper show, but the only audience were a couple of bemused drunks.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy in full lederhosen casually chatting with a busker wearing a beret outside Reuterplatz during a summer festival.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a 24-hour kebab shop next to a vintage vinyl store, both buzzing with a line out the door at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission if they still call it ‘the BART’ and know the quickest routes around all the construction traffic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading passengers on the 47 bus yesterday. Everyone was annoyed until he pulled out a sax. All of a sudden, we were in a jazz club.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists seem to think all bars serve tapas like they do in the guidebooks. In Gràcia, some spots serve only vermut and no food at all. Just drink and chat!

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll catch them fumbling with the metro map, eyes darting around like a tourist, and always standing on the left side of the escalator.
